title: Iran claims a hit on a US radar in Bahrain, Volgograd burns, and Europe gets a seat at the talks
summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards claim they destroyed a US radar in Bahrain while Central Command says it shot down the drones, Trump warns he would strike Iran with no hesitation, a Ukrainian drone attack kills four workers in Volgograd as Russian strikes kill three in Odesa and Zaporizhzhia, Zelensky says Europe will join the next round of talks, and Israeli strikes continue in Gaza and southern Lebanon.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Welcome to the ForceFinder Daily Briefing. I'm Avery.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And I'm Cole. As always, this show is generated automatically from the open-source reporting behind the ForceFinder map. Every story has source links on the globe, so treat us as a guide, not the final word.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: It's Friday, November thirteenth. And we start in the Gulf, with a claim that, if true, would be a serious escalation.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say they destroyed an American early-warning radar in Bahrain today. They called it retaliation for a strike on a telecom tower in Sirik, an Iranian town on the Strait of Hormuz.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: But the American account is very different. According to The New Arab, US Central Command denied the claim. It says US forces shot down two one-way attack drones heading for Bahrain, with no injuries and no damage.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And Bahrain hasn't confirmed any strike. So for now, the map records this as an attack that was intercepted, with Iran's claim noted as unverified.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Either way, it matters. Reuters notes it's the first time since early September that Iran has claimed an attack on American military assets in a Gulf country.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And the Guards added a warning. They said that if what they call aerial provocations and oil smuggling in the strait continue, they're ready to respond without limits.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: What about the strike that Iran says started it?

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Iran says an air attack hit that telecom tower in Sirik on Thursday. It blamed an unnamed enemy. Nobody has claimed it.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And this lands a day after some sharp words from Washington. On Thursday, President Trump said he would strike Iran again with, quote, no hesitation, if it threatens American allies or ships in the strait.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: On the Iranian side, the Assembly of Experts called for a review of Iran's membership of the nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty. That's a call from a clerical body, not a formal government decision. But it's a signal worth watching.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Put it together with this week. Tankers hit on three straight days. Iran's strike on navigation systems on Oman's Didamar Island. Now a claimed attack on a US site in Bahrain. The temperature in the Gulf is clearly rising.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Let's turn to Russia and Ukraine, where it was a deadly night on both sides of the border.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: In the Russian city of Volgograd, the regional governor, Andrei Bocharov, says four workers were killed and two were injured when Ukrainian drones attacked an industrial zone. He blamed the fires on falling debris.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Ukraine says it hit the Lukoil refinery there. That hasn't been officially confirmed on the Russian side. Russia's defence ministry says it shot down one thousand one hundred and ninety-eight Ukrainian drones overnight, which would be an enormous wave.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And that follows Kirishi, Ust-Luga and Omsk earlier in the week. Ukraine's campaign against Russia's oil industry isn't letting up.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: In Ukraine, the governor of the Odesa region, Oleh Kiper, says a Russian strike on a residential building killed two people and injured five.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: In Kyiv, debris from a drone set a medical facility on fire in the Shevchenkivskyi district. Staff evacuated thirty people, and rescuers pulled out seven more.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And in Zaporizhzhia, the acting governor says a strike killed a seventeen-year-old boy. The count of injured there has been climbing through the day. The regional governor put it at nineteen, and Kyiv Post later reported two dead and thirty injured. We'll update that figure as it firms up.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Now the diplomacy, and there is some movement. After meeting Putin in Moscow, the American envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, flew to Ireland and met President Zelensky at an airfield near Dublin.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Afterwards, Zelensky said two things. First, that Europe will be represented in the next round of talks. And second, that the prisoner exchange agreed in Abu Dhabi will be the largest of the war so far.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Kushner said Putin agreed to European participation. That's a shift, because earlier this week the Kremlin was ruling it out.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: But there's no date or venue yet. And on substance, the gap is still wide. CNN reports Putin stood firm on his territorial demands.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Kushner called the meeting with Zelensky a very good discussion, and Witkoff said another round is planned. But neither of them said which European countries would take part, or how.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: So the seat at the table is promised. The details are not.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: The Institute for the Study of War goes further. It assesses that Putin is refusing any demilitarized zone, and still demands the parts of four Ukrainian regions that Russian forces haven't taken.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: On the front line itself, the Institute says neither side advanced on Thursday. It also notes something technical but important. Ukrainian officials say speed restrictions on the Starshield satellite network are making it harder to intercept drones.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: To the rest of the Middle East. In Gaza, an Israeli strike on a vehicle outside a wedding hall in Deir al-Balah killed one Palestinian today, according to the Anadolu news agency.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And on Thursday's strike on Nasser Hospital, the United Nations now reports six killed and twenty-seven injured. The US-led Board of Peace, which oversees the ceasefire, urged both sides to uphold it.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: In southern Lebanon, Israeli artillery shelled five towns today, including Mayfadoun and Majdal Zoun, while drones flew low over Beirut without attacking. No casualties were reported.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And in Saudi Arabia, the coalition says it destroyed two Houthi drones on Thursday, aimed at Riyadh and the east of the country. The Houthis claim they hit oil facilities and military sites, and allege nearly a hundred Saudi strikes across Yemen in a day. None of that is verified.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: On the ships, still nothing confirmed. The Navy hasn't said when the Theodore Roosevelt will reach the Middle East, so its position on the map remains an estimate. Monday's fleet tracker should help. The George Washington and the George H. W. Bush are still the two carriers in the Arabian Sea.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: So, what to watch. Whether Washington responds to Iran's claimed attack in Bahrain, given Trump's warning. A date for the next round of Ukraine talks, with Europe in the room. And that prisoner exchange.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: That's the briefing. Thanks for listening, have a good weekend, and we'll see you tomorrow.
